title: Why the Pacers picked streaming service DAZN as regional broadcast partner
description: The Pacers announced on Thursday morning that they will be partnering with DAZN, a global sports streaming service based in London, as its TV partner.
fullText:
The Pacers' regional sports television rights have been in some form of limbo for more than three years since one broadcast partner went bankrupt and then the company that emerged in its place quickly found itself unable to make its rights payments.

So this offseason, after Main Street Sports Group -- the owner of the FanDuel Sports Network -- announced that it was winding down operations, the Pacers embarked on a search for a new regional broadcast partner and landed on one that takes a much different approach than the old model. This one does not have a traditional broadcast or cable channel and markets directly to the consumer, but it comes at a price.

The Pacers announced Thursday morning that they have entered into an agreement with the United Kingdom-based sports streaming company DAZN (pronounced Da-Zone) as its exclusive regional broadcast partner. Pacers fans who want to watch games on DAZN would have to download the company's streaming app, which could be done on any internet-connected devices including smart phones, laptops and smart televisions, but DAZN does not have a presence on any cable or satellite packages. The team announced that there will be 22 regular season games available for free on the DAZN app and that 15 of those games would also be expected to available on a local over-the-air broadcast partner. A local partner has not yet been chosen but Pacers executives say they expect to make that choice sometime in the next few weeks before the season starts.

Access to the rest of the games would require a season pass. Full price for the pass is $119.99 for the season, but fans who sign up before Oct. 15 can purchase an early-bird season pass for $59.99. A monthly pass will also be available for $19.99 per month. Season ticket holders will receive a free season pass. There will be a landing page on the DAZN app that will house all of Pacers content where fans will be directed to for subscription.

The Pacers will be in charge of the actual production of the broadcasts, meaning the announcers will remain the same. Chris Denari will be the play-by-play announcer for the 21st consecutive season, Quinn Buckner will be the color analyst, Jeremiah Johnson will be the sideline reporter and Eddie Gill will assist Johnson on the pregame, halftime and postgame shows while also maintaining his role as radio color analyst with Mark Boyle on play-by-play.

Pacers Sports and Entertainment CEO Mel Raines told reporters in an embargoed briefing Wednesday that the contract is a five-year deal, and though it gives the Pacers the opportunity to opt out in the future if the NBA puts together a regional sports television hub as it has been exploring, they could maintain the deal if the NBA and DAZN partner together on the hub, which is a possibility.

DAZN will be partnering with several of the 13 NBA teams whose rights became available when Main Street Sports Group effectively went under. The company already announced a partnership with the Minnesota Timberwolves and Raines indicated there will be more to come.

"When we were looking at partners -- and I should say, we probably talked to a dozen different options across the board -- one of the things we wanted to do was find somebody who we thought could be what the league refers to as their aggregated solution where you would aggregate all the teams," Raines said. "DAZN is certainly a top potential partner and that's been in the news. They were the only partner we were talking to who was going to potentially continue on. We are looking at this as a long-term partnership. It's a five-year deal, but ... the league required all the teams to have a potential out if there was an aggregated solution. We also don't have to necessarily opt into that. We're looking at this as we are happily in a five-year marriage with DAZN and hope the fans jump on board and love the service as much as we do."

Raines and Pacers Sports and Entertainment executive vice president and chief commercial officer Joey Graziano, who also met with the media Wednesday, said they tried to keep fans first and foremost in their thoughts when they were making their decision. They noted, however, that it's harder to please the entire fanbase now that sports and entertainment consumption have become so fragmented.

Graziano said that in their preparation, the Pacers learned that in 2010, almost 88% of households in the Pacers' designated market area had access to paid -- i.e. cable and satellite-- television. In 2026, that number has fallen to around 30%. The consistent trend of cord-cutting is a big reason why Diamond Sports Group -- which operated the Bally Sports Networks -- filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023 and the Main Street Sports Group that ran the Fan Duel Sports Networks had to effectively go out of business at the end of the 2025-26 NBA season. Graziano said that indicated that the Pacers had to pursue a digital-first strategy and market to fans through the internet rather than traditional linear television.

"We needed a solution that our fans could be able to access," Graziano said. "The way most of us are accessing our lives are via the internet in some way, having something that felt accessible across a variety of different modes and channels. That means your phone. That also may mean the tablet that you have. It may mean your gaming console. It may mean your smart television. We wanted something that would meet our fans exactly where they are as they're traveling in their busy lives."

Of course, not all of the Pacers' fans are in the same place and they know they'll have to deal with a portion of the fanbase that will not be pleased with this move. Their could be older fans without home access to the internet or fans who are already paying for television access who will be displeased to be asked to pay money for another subscription. The best the Pacers can do in that case, they noted, is try to be as accessible as possible in trying to guide those fans toward a new experience.

"Of course we're concerned about it," Graziano said. "We're concerned about all of our fans and we're going to be incredibly responsive to any concerns that come about for that. ... We've got to think about how we make sure those fans are able to We have an entire marketing and digital team who is hyper focused on fan feedback and we will be responsive to fan's concerns about their ability to access. That's an important part of our thought of how do you bring this together. There certainly will be some fans that may represent some challenges and as an organization we will address them."

Raines noted that the Pacers do not have access to some over-the-air opportunities that are available to others. Several teams, including the Bucks, Magic and Heat, have announced that they will broadcast all of their games on free over-the-air television this season. Raines said those teams were able to take advantage of effectively dead channels on their local packages that aren't available in the Indianapolis area.

"Some markets had the opportunity with a Scripps or a Grey to have an empty channel that is already bought into the lower tier of Comcast or Spectrum or DirecTV or Dish," Raines said. "That's not available in our market right now. As you know there's been a lot of consolidation. Unfortunately we didn't have that opportunity."

They also couldn't expect to ask a local broadcast affiliate of one of the big four national networks -- ABC, CBS, NBC and FOX -- to commit to showing all of the games that will not be broadcast nationally. The Pacers will appear on some form of national broadcast 11 times in their 82 regular season games -- once on ESPN, once on NBC, four times on Amazon Prime and five times on Peacock. Even getting 15 games over the air as they plan to, Raines said, is ambitious.

"They can't clear 71 games," Raines said. "They have network programming that they can't pre-empt 71 times. To get 15 at their peak season is difficult to be honest. If it was easy we'd be telling you who it was today. They have to navigate being able to pre-empt broadcast TV. There really isn't a single solution out there that hits 100% of the fans anymore or I'd tell you those 13 teams -- us being one of them -- would have already done that deal six months ago. That's what we're trying to do and I think our best shot at it is a partner like this."

DAZN has extensive experience with this situation, especially overseas, and the company was aggressive in courting the 13 teams that had partnered with Main Street. Raines said DAZN was the only potential partner that wanted to come to Indiana for an in-person meeting. Zander Berlinksi, DAZN's senior vice president of strategy and business development, also attended Wednesday's press briefing.

According to the press release announcing the partnership, DAZN streams more than 140,000 live events annually and is available in more than 200 markets worldwide. The United States overall market accounts for a relatively small percentage of its business, but it partners with some of the biggest sports leagues in Europe and Japan, and also serves as a global distributor for U.S. sports leagues. Berlinski said DAZN owns the exclusive rights to Italy's Serie A soccer league and Spain's La Liga as well as much of the domestic baseball in Japan. It also, according to Berlinski, is the largest partner for the NFL internationally outside of the U.S. and China as it platforms NFL Game Pass internationally.

"Over the last 10 years, we've built a tremendous tech platform that is powered by 2,000-plus engineers that is purpose-built for sports," Berlinski said, "and has experienced working with teams and leagues across the world to help grow audiences."

Dustin Dopirak covers the Pacers all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Pacers Insider newsletter.

title: Young Eagles player got treated like a ‘piñata doll’—but his coach won’t give up on him
description: Young Eagles defender still has hope.
fullText:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — Eagles cornerback Kelee Ringo failed to hold onto a starting job last season. The struggles Ringo experienced during his three starts made him the target of criticism from fans and media alike.

This summer, Ringo has been taking reps with the Eagles' second- and third-team defensive units. The 2023 fourth-round pick is competing to be one of the team's top backups, and last week, he made a statement by snagging an interception in the Eagles' preseason loss to the Baltimore Ravens.

"I think Kelee is— he's been everybody's piñata doll for a while," Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said before Wednesday's joint practice against the Patriots. "I kind of sense he could be coming. We'll see."

Eagles coach pumps the brakes on beloved young player: 'He didn't play the right way'Aug. 20, 2026, 6:15 a.m.

Eagles' stock up, stock down after Day 1 vs. Patriots: Major addition living up to 'sloppy' labelAug. 20, 2026, 7:36 a.m.

Fangio gives honest reviews of his players. On the same day, he said that Eagles defensive tackle Ty Robinson had "been on life support" for most of his career. His review of Ringo was much more positive.

Ringo is not a roster lock, but Fangio's belief in him is a good sign for his chances of making the team. If he makes the team, Ringo will be playing in the final year of his rookie deal in 2026.

"I think these two days [of joint practices] for him are big," Fangio said.

title: 'We don't have a point to prove to anyone' - Van Dijk
description: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted last season's title defence was "unacceptable", but he believes the players "have an opportunity to turn it around" under new head coach Andoni Iraola.  The Reds still qualified for Champions League football despite finishing fifth in the Premier League last season with 60 points.  "We all know how tough it will be, but if you aren't up for the challenge then you aren't at the right place," Van Dijk said.
fullText:
Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted last season's title defence was "unacceptable", but he believes the players "have an opportunity to turn it around" under new head coach Andoni Iraola.

The Reds still qualified for Champions League football despite finishing fifth in the Premier League last season with 60 points.

"We all know how tough it will be, but if you aren't up for the challenge then you aren't at the right place," Van Dijk said. "What I feel at the moment is everybody is up for the challenge.

"Let's see how we go about it. I'm really looking forward to this season.

"I don't feel we have a point to prove to anyone. We just have to show how much we care, how much we want to fight for this badge and also realise how privileged we are to be playing for Liverpool."

The 35-year-old will welcome better cover in central defence this season, with Liverpool signing Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo while Giovanni Leoni is close to a return from an ACL injury

There will also be a new style of play under Iraola, who won plaudits for his brand of football during his time at Bournemouth.

"If you look at Bournemouth last season, they were pretty exciting," Van Dijk added. "If we keep working, believing and showing our quality, we can be very excited.

"We need everyone to be fit. We need a squad that is able to compete on all four fronts, that's the only way to try to be successful.

"Let's see what the last couple weeks of the transfer window brings and then let's go for it."

title: Spain break 23-year-old international cricket record held by Ricky Ponting and Steve Waugh's Australia
description: Spain are currently playing in the Men's T20 World Cup Sub Regional Europe Qualifiers in Southern Finland and have won all their matches in the tournament so far. Their latest victory came against Bulgaria on August 18, when they chased down a target of 60 in just 29 deliveries, winning by nine wickets.
fullText:
Not Australia, England, India or Pakistan. Spain have become the team with the longest winning streak in international cricket, breaking the record previously held by Ricky Ponting and Steve Waugh's Australia.

Spain are currently playing in the Men's T20 World Cup Sub Regional Europe Qualifiers in Southern Finland and have won all their matches in the tournament so far. Their latest victory came against Bulgaria on August 18, when they chased down a target of 60 in just 29 deliveries, winning by nine wickets.

Spain moved past Australia's record when they beat Finland in their opening match on August 14. That victory was their 21st in a row in international cricket, taking them one win beyond Australia's previous record of 20.

They have since extended the streak to 24 consecutive victories after beating the Isle of Man, Luxembourg and Bulgaria.

Spain's 24-match winning run has included T20I series against the Isle of Man and Jersey, as well as two series against Croatia. The two Croatia series were separated by the ICC Men's T20 World Cup Sub Regional Europe Qualifier in 2024, where Spain finished second after one of their matches was abandoned.

How Australia's record was setAustralia's previous record of 20 consecutive international wins came across Tests and ODIs under Waugh and Ponting.

The run began on January 11, 2003, when Australia beat England in Hobart. It continued until the third Test against the West Indies in Bridgetown in May 2003.

Australia's winning run finally ended when the Waugh-led side lost the fourth Test against the West Indies.

During that period, Australia went unbeaten in the 2003 ODI World Cup after winning all their matches in a tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka. They then switched to Test cricket and won three matches against the West Indies.

Ponting captained Australia in the ODI tri-series and the World Cup, while Waugh led the team in Tests.

Australia played 17 ODIs and three Tests during their 20-match winning streak.

Spain have now gone past that mark, extending their international winning run to 24 matches.

title: What you need to know about girls soccer in the St. Cloud metro this fall
description: Who's good? Who still needs work? Here is everything you need to know about girls soccer in the St. Cloud metro this fall.
fullText:
ST. CLOUD, MN — The soccer season is right around the corner, and there are a handful of girls' soccer squads with high hopes going into the season. Others might just wish to see the ball go into the net in each game.

Starting with the best the St. Cloud metro has to offer:

2025 record: 18-3-1, Class 1A co-third place finish

Top returners: F Amelia Newiger, F Nora Simones, F/GK Jordan Bovy

While not quite as dominant in recent years as their boys team counterparts, the girls over at Cathedral have certainly impressed in their own regard with three consecutive seasons without a conference loss, and most recently a co-third place finish at the state tournament.

Going into this year, there should not be much doubt about if the Crusaders can make another deep state run. They return their top two goalscorers in Newiger and Simones, the latter of which also led the team in assists. Although Cathedral will be losing out on the sure hands of Aubrey Lesnau in goal, Bovy posted a .872 save percentage in relief last season and contributed seven goals and eight assists when on the pitch.

Cathedral will take on Southwest Christian at home on Aug. 28 to start its season.

Check out the boys soccer preview here: What you need to know about boys soccer in the St. Cloud metro this fall

2025 record: 13-6, Section 8 champions

Top returners: F Mollie Statsick, F Rosabella Castillo, GK Mya Ramirez

The Sabres breezed past their Section 8 foes last season with a combined score of 12-0 across the three games, which was a theme all season long. If they knew they were better, they flat-out proved it: 10-1 win against Willmar, 9-0 vs. Sauk Rapids, 8-1 vs. Rocori and 7-1 vs. Fergus Falls. In their 13 wins, the average margin of victory was five goals.

While Sartell loses a bulk of its production from last season, getting Statsick back is really all the talent the Sabres need. The forward netted 37 goals to break the school record and added 14 assists to lead her squad.

Ramirez will be stepping into goal as a sophomore but showed a strong .778 save percentage in her 150 minutes of relief as a freshman last season. Only time will tell if that mark can last through a full season.

Sartell starts its quest towards a repeat state tournament appearance on Aug. 27 against Anoka.

Top returners: F Adele Changamire, M Andersyn Changamire, M Alyssa Kinney

A young team last season, the Bulldogs welcome back virtually all their production, led by their top two goal scorers in the Changamire sisters. Adele, the elder sister, found the back of the net 33 times while leading the team with 12 assists; Andersyn logged 19 goals and 11 assists of her own.

Kinney, one of the few seniors with contribution last year, provided nine assists and two goals.

Starting the season 0-2 last year, the young Becker squad really caught stride to go 10-1-3 down the stretch before Monticello, who the Bulldogs drew a tie with during the regular season, bested them 3-1 in the Section 6 semifinals. Now an older and more developed squad, certainly do not be surprised if Becker advances through to the state tournament this season.

Becker starts the season with five consecutive home matches, starting with Southwest Christian on Aug. 29.

Becker has two on this list: Who are the top returning offensive players in the St. Cloud metro?

Top returners: M Claudia Ruzanic, F Lauren Lenzmeir, M/GK Maya Beumer

Despite fielding an incredibly young lineup last season, including seventh grader Sofia Sommers and eighth grader Lucy Gardner, the Johnnies put together an impressive 10-win season that was eventually ended by Cathedral in sectionals.

Aside from the impressive youngsters, St. John's returns its top two leading goal scorers in Ruzanic and Lezmeir while returning Beumer in goal, who shined with a .811 save percentage.

While it is certainly unfortunate for the Johnnies to be in the same section as Cathedral, if development stays on track, it is a matter of when, not if, they make it to the state tournament over the next few seasons.

The Johnnies start their season on Aug. 27 against East Grand Forks.

Top returners: M Isabella Frantesl, GK Reeghan Stevens

The Crush had a fun season in their inaugural year as a girls soccer co-op, which was ultimately ended by Sartell in the sectional championship.

A senior-heavy squad last season, it will be hard to replace the production being lost. However, returning their second-leading goal scorer in Frantesl sets her up for a big senior season with the amount of scoring that was lost. Boasting a .865 save percentage as a freshman, getting Stevens back in goal for the next three years is a luxury most teams cannot afford. A standout athlete in golf and hockey as well, she logged four shutouts for the Crush.

St. Cloud will start its quest back to the sectional championship on the road Aug. 27 against Marshall with its home-opener on Aug. 29 against Osseo.

Top returners: F/M Ashley Storms, F Emelia Terwey, F Jasmie Perez

Graduating seven seniors in the spring, Rocori will be losing top goal scorer Sophia Hennen and goalkeeper Abby Stewart. However, the Spartans do retain their next three highest goal scorers, which accounts for the bulk of their scoring production.

Storms netted nine goals, Terwey with seven and Perez scored four of her own as just a seventh grader last year.

With the bulk of the talent loss being on the defensive half, the Spartans will certainly have a lot of holes to fill. Nonetheless, with the scoring they get back another winning season is likely in the books.

They start on the road Aug. 27 against Bemidji and have their home opener Aug. 31 against East Grand Forks.

Top returners: GK Stephanie Pelzer, F Hope Anderson, M Riley Rushmeyer

Albany graduated nine players last spring, which is not always the worst-case scenario with the outcomes said senior class brought. Regardless, the Huskies did have some promising efforts throughout the season including a 2-1 win over Walker-Hackensack-Akeley (10-6-1) and a 1-0 loss to St. John's in sectionals.

The Huskies return just two seniors in Pelzer and Anderson, who will be able to provide a veteran presence to a rather inexperienced team that will have a lot of juniors playing for the first time. Rushmeyer is one of few from the 2028 class that contributed last season.

Albany starts its season on the road on Aug. 27 against Detroit Lakes and will have its home-opener on Aug. 31 against Sartell.

Top returners: M Sydney Bauer, F Scarlett Bauer

There really is no hiding the fact that the Storm just simply were not a good team last year; they scored four goals all year and got shut out 11 times. They did draw a tie against a strong Rocori team but also surrendered a 2-0 halftime lead that game.

Regardless, a new year means a fresh slate for a team certainly would rather forget last season happened.

SRRHS only graduates four and get back half of their season production with the Bauer sisters. Time will tell how this season pans out, but sometimes all a roster needs is continuity and time to develop.

Sauk Rapids starts the season at home on Aug. 28 against Little Falls.

You can reach St. Cloud Times sports reporter David Jacobs and send story ideas to djacobs@gannett.com and follow him on X, formally known as Twitter, @davidrjacobs10.

title: Verstappen hopes F1 going in right direction as he signs Red Bull deal
description: Max Verstappen has been convinced by Formula One bosses over the direction of the sport after ending speculation about his future by signing a new long-term deal with Red Bull. The four-time world champion's future has dominated the agenda throughout the season amid Red Bull's indifferent form and his bitter unhappiness at the sport's new regulations.
fullText:
Max Verstappen has been convinced by Formula One bosses over the direction of the sport after ending speculation about his future by signing a new long-term deal with Red Bull.

The four-time world champion's future has dominated the agenda throughout the season amid Red Bull's indifferent form and his bitter unhappiness at the sport's new regulations.

But on Thursday, ahead of his home race in Zandvoort this weekend, Red Bull announced that the Dutchman had signed a deal until 2030.

The Dutchman has been the fiercest critic of the sport's new rules, which see a 50-50 split between electrical and internal combustion engine (ICE) power, even suggesting he may walk away from F1.

Changes have been announced for the next two seasons, with more power being generated by the ICE, while FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has expressed his desire to bring a V8 engine back to the sport in 2030 - for the first time since 2013.

"I love racing and I had a lot of very good discussions with F1 and the FIA and I think we are slowly working towards something that becomes better and better," Verstappen told a news conference.

"From my side, I adapted. I accepted the situation we are in - I am not happy with it - but the conversations I had with F1 and FIA are trying to make little improvements for next year and the year after.

"Plus the year that I signed to leaving the door open for a potential V8 return. I'm willing to accept that at the moment it is not fantastic but I still love racing.

"It is still an F1 car. This is still the pinnacle of motorsport and I want to be here."

Verstappen had been linked with a sensational switch to Mercedes and McLaren as well as a possible exit from the sport.

"I think I was closer to retiring than changing teams," he added.

Verstappen fell just short of a fifth successive world championship last season, losing out to Lando Norris at the final race, but has yet to win in 2026 and is sixth in the standings - 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli.

His previous Red Bull contract ran until 2028, with performance-related break clauses offering him a potential exit, but the team and F1 bosses will be pleased to have secured Verstappen's commitment.

The 28-year-old expressed his desire to finish his career with the UK-based team, with whom he started in F1 as a 17-year-old in 2015.

"You need to feel good where you're at. I feel very good in this team, I have the belief in the people that we can get back to the top. Time will tell," Verstappen said.

"I still want to win races, I am hungry to win more, plus Red Bull allows me to do things outside of F1. So the whole package is a big plus.

"I like it here. It would be a great story if that were possible - being picked up by Red Bull and finishing your career in one team. I don't feel the need to change just to change or drive in another colour. It would be an amazing story."

Team principal Laurent Mekies said: "Having Max continue with us and retaining the best driver on the grid is fantastic news for everyone at Red Bull, Oracle Red Bull Racing, as well as F1 and motorsport as a whole.

"The decision to continue our journey together is rooted in the trust Max and the team have built over many years, as well as Max's confidence in our people, our culture and our vision for the future."

title: 'Fortress Portman Road is going to be key'
description: Ipswich Town chief executive and chairman Mark Ashton has praised new head coach Gary O'Neil's impact at the club since his appointment in June.  It has been a busy summer at Portman Road as the chief executive has orchestrated player recruitment, stadium developments and a new training ground.  From safe standing, an extension to fan facilities and improvements made to accessibility improvements, the Tractor Boys have made changes aimed at making Portman Road a "fortress".
fullText:
Ipswich Town chief executive and chairman Mark Ashton has praised new head coach Gary O'Neil's impact at the club since his appointment in June.

Speaking to BBC Radio Suffolk's Brenner Woolley, Ashton said: "We have still got work to do, but I certainly think he is fitting in well.

"His work-ethic, his morale and the way he interacts with people is first class."

It has been a busy summer at Portman Road as the chief executive has orchestrated player recruitment, stadium developments and a new training ground.

From safe standing, an extension to fan facilities and improvements made to accessibility improvements, the Tractor Boys have made changes aimed at making Portman Road a "fortress".

"The team was really good, but the fans were outstanding [last season]," added Ashton.

"We have got a group of new players who have never experienced what Portman Road can do. Fortress Portman Road is going to be key."

As well as the £150m Ipswich have spent on new players, the club has invested £30m into training ground developments, which Ashton says was inspired by former Town boss Sir Bobby Robson's advice when he was Newcastle manager.

"He was saying: 'Mark, look, the training ground has to be elite. It has to be a place of work. Don't build a spa facility. Don't build a leisure centre. Build something which is functional and elite.'

"Those words have stayed with me - 20-25 years on I have had the opportunity to deliver what he told me about at his football club."

Although it has been a busy summer transfer window, Ashton confirmed Ipswich "are not done" as they look to sign more players before the deadline on 1 September.

title: Notre Dame Football and the Transfer Portal Noise
description: The transfer portal is a big part of Notre Dame and college football, and its impact on the sport is constant.
fullText:
Sometimes it's better to have more than one or two options… so use the triple option.

Former Notre Dame quarterback, Brady Quinn, bleeds blue and gold. The Dublin, Ohio, native has been one of the most popular faces of Notre Dame football over the last two decades, and has represented Notre Dame well in his various roles with the media. Recently he was asked about the transfer portal and what he might have done if the portal was in place after Ty Willingham was fired. It's about as honest of an answer that you're going to hear.

Transfer portal. NIL. Realignment. Would @Brady_Quinn have stayed at Notre Dame in today's CFB landscape? pic.twitter.com/Ivt52Cd7nF

Notre Dame defensive lineman, Armel Mukam, entered the transfer portal during the offseason. Mukam had barely played in South Bend and was looking for a fresh start. Notre Dame, however, made sure to re-recruit Mukam as their own need for defensive linemen increased during the offseason. In the end, Armel chose to stay at Notre Dame and through spring and summer — it looks like it might be paying off for him and the Irish.

"Last year, I don't think he could have played here. This year, a whole flip switched in him. I don't even know how to explain it, but something flipped in him and he's just playing out of his mind right now."

— Jaylen Sneed on Armel Mukam (88)https://t.co/SPxYV4ro8e pic.twitter.com/6nbAUWtRvB

Notre Dame did a fantastic job in the transfer portal by grabbing Ohio State wide receivers, Quincy Porter and Mylan Graham. And yet… it's Jaden Greenhouse, Micah Gilbert, and a pair of lacrosse bros in Jordan Faison and Matt Jeffery that have made the most noise at WR so far this fall camp.

Notre Dame lost two first-round NFL Draft picks from its backfield, which could put even more emphasis on the passing game… and OC Mike Denbrock has shown he isn't afraid to air it out.

Here’s a quick look at Jaden Greathouse, an emerged leader, and Ohio State transfer Mylan… pic.twitter.com/jRHTwKWCwj

We have entered an entirely new wold with college football, and the legal cases along the way are reshaping much of what may happen this season. Recently, a judge ordered that 15 players that have entered NFL training camps as rookies, may return to college football this season and use the transfer portal to find a new home. Former Notre Dame defensive lineman, Junior Tuihalamaka, is among those listed. Seeing as he is a part of THIS particular lawsuit, Irish fans should expect him to play elsewhere in 2026.

NEW: Buccaneers EDGE Jack Pyburn and 15 others have been granted a TRO for a fifth year of College Football, @PeteNakos reports. 

Pyburn posted 2 sacks in Tampa Bay's last preseason game. https://t.co/ig9JbrwsGC pic.twitter.com/ByK5y4W3rq

title: Steelers insider reveals harsh truth about Max Iheanachor
description: One respected insider argued that Pittsburgh Steelers rookie offensive tackle Max Iheanachor won't see time in a starting position anytime soon.
fullText:
The offensive line remains a huge question mark for the new-look Pittsburgh Steelers, and despite spending premium draft capital on a highly touted offensive tackle, one insider believes a starting position isn't in the cards quite yet.

While first-round rookie Max Iheanachor looked impressive to kick off training camp, Steelers insider Mark Kaboly argued his recent injury setback all but dashed any hopes of earning the starting job at right tackle for Week 1.

"He has zero chance to be the starter Week 1, 0.1 percent chance," Kaboly said via his podcast. "He just missed too much time. You can't make up two weeks in pads at training camp as a rookie who needed a lot of reps. And you miss all those reps then all of a sudden think you're gonna be able to start a Week 1 game. Maybe not 0.1 percent, but a low percentage of him having any chance of starting early in the season. October, maybe."

Iheanachor, who won some promising one-on-one reps versus the likes of T.J. Watt, Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer, unfortunately suffered a neck/shoulder injury two weeks ago. He's missed practice since the setback and could miss the Steelers' remaining two preseason games as he recovers.

Dylan Cook finished last season as a capable starting left tackle but was asked to switch to the right side in 2026. He, like Troy Fautanu, who moved to the left side, hasn't really acclimated well to the change. Cook's struggles could open the door for Iheanachor to get a shot at the starting job sooner rather than later. But as Kaboly pointed out, it probably won't happen before Week 1.

title: 3 noteworthy moments in Aryna Sabalenka’s Cincinnati Open loss
description: The happy-go-lucky Aryna Sabalenka days are temporarily in the past. Sabalenka lost in shocking manner to 20-year-old Sara Bejlek in the Cincinnati Open Round of 16 in a match that concluded after midnight on Thursday, August 20. Sabalenka has not…
fullText:
The happy-go-lucky Aryna Sabalenka days are temporarily in the past. Sabalenka lost in shocking manner to 20-year-old Sara Bejlek in the Cincinnati Open Round of 16 in a match that concluded after midnight on Thursday, August 20.

Sabalenka has not won a tennis tournament since becoming the fifth woman ever to sweep the Sunshine Double of Indian Wells and Miami in March. She has looked more vulnerable lately indicating her confidence and game are not where she wants them to be going into the US Open. She even told Tennis Channel that the Cincinnati Open is her opportunity to "reset."

Hardcourts are where she thrives, but she was not feeling comfortable at 3 noteworthy times in the Bejlek match.

MORE: Aryna Sabalenka stunned by Sara Bejlek at Cincinnati Open

It is not uncommon for players to toss their racquets on the ground in frustration. Sabalenka did it, and the little piece on the racquet, known as the vibration dampener, fell off and was lost.

The ballkids were looking in the area where the photographers were positioned, and this caused a delay despite the fact that Sabalenka ultimately used another out of her bag.

No delay of game penalty assessed in this unusual circumstance.

Sabalenka's body language emitted frustration. She impatiently waited for a ballkid to give her a ball. At one point, she angrily bounced a ball back to the person.

Tennis Channel said nothing. Only Brett Haber could be heard murmurring, "hmm."

Aug 19, 2026; Mason, OH, USA; Aryna Sabalenka reacts after returning a shot against Sara Bejlek (CZE) during the Cincinnati Open at Lindner Family Tennis Center. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images

MORE: Simona Halep, berated by Nick Kyrgios in the past, speaks out about his cocaine-related suspension

Sabalenka is not the most gracious in defeat. There have been previous examples.

Of course, she was disappointed and unhappy, but as WTA World No. 1, she could have acknowledged Bejlek's breakthrough moment with a little more finesse.

Everyone has a bad day on the court, and Sabalenka's high level of consistency and play over the past couple of years are spectacular achievements that some of us took for granted. Getting deep into every tournament she was in, winning many, means she has played a lot of tennis.

Maybe that wear and tear is taking its toll. She is a fighter and will use this unexpected downtime to be even more prepared for the upcoming US Open.

In the meantime, Czechia, home of Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, has yet another talented player and star in the making in Sara Bejlek.

title: Johann Zarco set to return at Aragon GP after terrifying Barcelona accident
description: More than one hundred days after suffering a crash at the Catalan GP, the French rider received clearance from his personal doctors to attempt a comeback at MotorLand next week
fullText:
LCR has announced that Johann Zarco will make his MotoGP comeback at the Aragon Grand Prix, which is due to take place from 28-30 August, provided he passes a medical evaluation next Thursday.

Zarco suffered a horrifying crash at Turn 1 during the first restart at the Catalan Grand Prix in May. In the accident, which also involved Luca Marini and Francesco Bagnaia, Zarco's left leg became caught in the rear wheel of the latter's Ducati, and he suffered a nasty ligament injury in his knee as well as a deep burn in the same area.

Initially, the doctors opted to wait for the inflammation in his knee to go down and for the burn to recover before operating on him, but as the days went by, the diagnosis by doctor Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet and his team in Lyon changed to conservative treatment, with Zarco avoiding surgery and LCR announcing a possible return in September.

However, according to Honda's satellite team, "Johann's recovery has progressed favourably in recent weeks, which has allowed him to bring forward his return to the track."

In the same statement, it added that Zarco "has progressively increased his workload, riding both a supermotard and a Honda CBR1000RR as part of his rehabilitation", as Motorsport.com previously reported on 7 August.

The conclusion is that "after having progressed steadily and having received clearance from his medical team to return to racing, Zarco will travel to Aragon with the aim of returning to competition, subject to passing the mandatory medical evaluation at the circuit."

Zarco has already spent 96 days out of action since suffering his injury on 17 May, a period in which he missed six grands prix: Italy, Hungary, the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Germany and Great Britain. If he returns for FP1 at the Aragon GP on 28 August, he will have been sidelined for more than 100 days.

During that stretch of races, LCR counted on the formidable contribution of British rider Cal Crutchlow, who made a surprise comeback after retiring from MotoGP in 2020. The 40-year-old failed to score any points in any of the six weekends he took part in, but he came very close in Hungary and the Netherlands, where he crossed the finish line in 16th.

Although LCR has full confidence in Zarco's recovery, everything indicates that Crutchlow will travel to Aragon in case the Frenchman is unable to pass the medical examination performed by Dr Angel Charte at the circuit. Crutchlow is also understood to be focusing on his fitness for the rest of the season in case his services are required again in any of the ten remaining grands prix this season.

title: Bernardo Silva opens up on Real Madrid move and Mbappe connection: ‘A class act’
description: Bernardo Silva has opened up on his move to Real Madrid, describing the opportunity to join the Spanish giants as a dream come true while also revealing his excitement at reuniting with Kylian Mbappe....
fullText:
Bernardo Silva has opened up on his move to Real Madrid, describing the opportunity to join the Spanish giants as a dream come true while also revealing his excitement at reuniting with Kylian Mbappe.

The Portuguese midfielder spoke to Real Madrid TV following his welcome ceremony at Real Madrid City, covering everything from his relationship with Mbappe to his first impressions of the dressing room and his ambitions for the new season.

For Bernardo, the move to the Santiago Bernabeu did not require much thought.

"When Real Madrid called me, I didn't hesitate.

"When they rang and told me they were interested, I said yes straight away, without a second thought, because I believe it's the best option for me, for my career and for my family. Being here is a dream come true."

One of the most interesting parts of Bernardo's arrival at Real Madrid is his reunion with Mbappe.

The two previously played together at Monaco, where they formed part of a hugely talented young side before taking their careers to different destinations.

Bernardo still remembers the connection they developed during those two seasons.

"We played together for two years at Monaco. He was very young – he was 17 or 18. I was very young too.

"We had a very strong connection as teammates. Since then, we've played against each other quite a few times – against Paris, against France and against Madrid.

"Now I'm really happy to be back with him and to try and rekindle that connection.

"Kylian is a class act, a player who can single-handedly win you matches, who scores plenty of goals and creates lots of chances in every game.

"We'll try to work on rebuilding that connection so that, together, we can bring joy to Real Madrid."

Bernardo also spoke warmly about Florentino Perez and the history he has built during his time as Real Madrid president.

"I was speaking to the president, who took over in 2000.

"I've followed his entire journey at Real Madrid and, with him as president, the club has won seven Champions League titles, which is a lot. Now, being able to play for him and for this club is really special."

Bernardo has wasted little time settling into his new surroundings.

According to the midfielder, the atmosphere inside the Real Madrid dressing room has impressed him, with the squad already focused on competing for silverware across every competition.

"The dressing room atmosphere is great. Everyone gets on really well and we're really keen to do well.

"We're very ambitious about winning every trophy and we're confident we have the squad to do it.

"I feel we're a strong group, with a great bond and a real hunger to win – which is what you're supposed to do at a club like Real Madrid."

Bernardo also made a clear promise about what Real Madrid supporters can expect from him.

"I'm a different player to when I started my career, but I'm very happy with the path I've taken and with who I am today – the player that Real Madrid fans can expect.

"I can promise that I'm a hard-working player who will always put the team before my own interests; for me, that's the most important thing.

"I hope that in every match, through the good times and the bad, everyone can see that I'm giving my all. I'll leave everything on the pitch, and that I can certainly promise."

He knows the challenge of playing at the Santiago Bernabeu better than most after facing Real Madrid several times during his career.

"It's been very difficult to play at the Bernabeu and now I hope it'll be the other way round – that it'll be very easy.

"It's undoubtedly one of the most impressive stadiums – if not the most impressive – you can play in."

Despite the excitement surrounding his presentation, Bernardo is already looking ahead to Real Madrid's La Liga opener against Espanyol.

The midfielder stressed that the team cannot afford to treat any fixture lightly if they want to challenge for the league title.

"I hope we win. We need to stay focused in every match. Every point counts. LaLiga is a competition where you can't afford to drop too many points if you want to be champions.

"We have to attach just as much importance to the points in matches that people perhaps regard as slightly less significant than the big games.

"We'll try to get off to a strong start, with a win and the three points," he concluded.

title: Duran's 'world-class' performance in numbers
description: Camilo Duran has wasted little time in becoming a Celtic hero.  The 24-year-old Colombian delivered what Martin O'Neill hailed as a "world-class" performance in the 3-0 win over LASK that pushed Celtic to the brink of the Champions League.  Duran's brilliant double had Parkhead bouncing while his tireless workrate and eagerness to track back also had fans nodding in approval.
fullText:
Camilo Duran has wasted little time in becoming a Celtic hero.

The 24-year-old Colombian delivered what Martin O'Neill hailed as a "world-class" performance in the 3-0 win over LASK that pushed Celtic to the brink of the Champions League.

Duran's brilliant double had Parkhead bouncing while his tireless workrate and eagerness to track back also had fans nodding in approval. Could he even be an upgrade on departed idol Daizen Maeda?

"We know how important Maeda was to Celtic winning the league last season with his workrate, willingness to press and run in behind, and coming up with goals in big moments," said former Scotland forward James McFadden.

"Duran is showing he has all those attributes - and a little bit more. Outstanding - and the frightening thing is he's playing out of position."

On a night where Celtic had no passengers in a breathless performance - while riding their luck at times - it was Duran who shone brightest and his numbers underline his effectiveness.

He netted two goals from a combined xG of just 0.46, showing lethal finishing as he thumped in a volley then arced home either side of half-time.

In total Duran, who was deployed on the right wing, attempted six shots - the most of any Celtic player - and put four on target, while his five touches in the opposition box was a joint high with Kasper Hogh.

Duran also ranked joint first across both teams for dribbles (six, tied with Yang Hyun-jun) and won possession five times, a tally bettered only by Callum McGregor.

As captain McGregor remarked post-match: "Two unbelieves finishes - he's looked a real, real threat. But the thing I love the most about him is his workrate."

title: Bill Belichick’s new quarterback receives unflattering ACC ranking
description: Bill Belichick selected Billy Edwards Jr. to lead North Carolina, but preseason ACC rankings reveal considerable skepticism about the decision.
fullText:
Bill Belichick's new quarterback receives unflattering ACC ranking originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Bill Belichick made his choice at quarterback. Outside expectations for that choice remain modest. North Carolina named Billy Edwards Jr. its starter for the 2026 season opener against TCU, giving the experienced transfer responsibility for reviving an offense that struggled throughout Belichick's debut season.

USA Today subsequently placed Edwards in the bottom tier of its preseason ACC quarterback rankings, a sobering assessment for a Tar Heels program attempting to rebound from a 4-8 finish.

The ranking reflects the uncertainty surrounding Edwards more than a complete lack of ability. He has proven capable of producing at the Power Four level, but a knee injury cost him nearly the entire 2025 season at Wisconsin.

Belichick now is betting that a healthy Edwards can recapture his previous form.

Edwards won North Carolina's competition over Texas A&M transfer Miles O'Neill and will start against TCU on Aug. 29 in Dublin, Ireland. The sixth-year quarterback brings substantially more experience than his competition. Edwards started 11 games for Maryland in 2024, completing 65% of his passes for 2,881 yards, 15 touchdowns and nine interceptions. He also has displayed value as a runner throughout his college career.

His anticipated opportunity at Wisconsin ended almost immediately. Edwards injured his knee during the 2025 opener and attempted only 16 passes all season. That lost year explains some of the skepticism entering his North Carolina debut.

Multiple preseason evaluations have positioned Edwards near the bottom of the ACC's quarterback hierarchy. CBS Sports ranked him 14th among the conference's projected starters, while other outlets have placed him in a similar range. The repeated doubts give Belichick and Edwards an obvious opportunity to outperform expectations.

MORE: Paul Finebaum unloads on Dabo Swinney with brutal message before Clemson-LSU showdown

Belichick overhauled his quarterback room after North Carolina's disappointing first season under the former New England Patriots coach. The Tar Heels also hired Bobby Petrino as offensive coordinator, creating an intriguing partnership between two of football's most experienced and recognizable coaches. Petrino's history of developing quarterbacks could help Edwards make the most of his final college season.

North Carolina needs immediate improvement.

The Tar Heels finished 4-8 in Belichick's first year and opened that season with a humbling 48-14 loss to TCU. The rematch in Ireland gives the program an opportunity to demonstrate that its extensive offseason changes produced meaningful progress.

Edwards does not need to become the ACC's best quarterback for North Carolina to improve. He must remain healthy, protect the football and provide stability to an offense that rarely found it last season.

His placement in the conference's bottom tier nevertheless underscores the size of Belichick's gamble.

Miami's Darian Mensah, NC State's C.J. Bailey and SMU's Kevin Jennings enter the season with established production and significant expectations. Edwards enters with a surgically repaired knee, a new offense and plenty to prove.

Belichick has built his career around finding value where others see limitations. His new quarterback now represents the latest test of that philosophy. If Edwards exceeds his modest preseason billing, North Carolina could become one of the ACC's biggest surprises. If the ranking proves accurate, Belichick's second season might resemble his first.

title: These Are The College Football Games You Miss Your Own Wedding For
description: The biggest games in college football in 2026—the ones so must-see, you’d miss your own wedding to watch them. Rivalries, stars and playoff stakes.
fullText:
Being a college football fanatic is a tough business. Watch parties, road trips, tailgating or just taking up the couch for an entire Saturday are just some of the options. From a happily married (about to be tested) man's perspective, I must navigate the better half's plans that don't include me watching television for 14 hours straight. To me it's non-negotiable.

In reality it's a non-negotiable negotiation. I often lose but I fight the good fight.

There's a major game with playoff implications every week. Conference games are must see. Being laser focused on a 2nd-and-11 from your own 23 while avoiding the side eye is an art. Master your craft fellas. To help I've identified five (for now) can't miss games that will directly impact the season. Blackout dates for doing anything else, if you will. Futures odds from various sources.

Two weeks in to the season and we've got a banger. There's nothing like a top five matchup early. In the old days this would be an elimination game. This year it's for playoff position, bragging rights and some Heisman hype.

Arch Manning and Julian Sayin are going to be trading favorite status all season long. Whoever wins this game gains nothing on that front. Hopefully, this won't be a snoozer like last year. This game is in Austin and given the spread the Buckeyes would be a slight favorite at a neutral site. As talented as Texas is, I believe Ohio State brings enough offense to keep this close.

Prediction: Texas scores last and wins. Take the under and lay the points.

Alabama will be in the top 10 by the time this game rolls around (not entirely confident about this). Georgia will be where they usually are. This is one of, if not the best, SEC matchups this year. Texas-LSU and Texas-Oklahoma could prove to have much more at stake as the season rolls on but for now it's Bulldogs-Tide.

Alabama still hasn't named a starter at quarterback though it looks as if Keelon Russell is on track to win the job over Austin Mack. Gunner Stockton returns as Georgia's quarterback and leader. Advantage Bulldogs. My confidence in Alabama's offense is shaky at best. The home crowd keeps this game close but Georgia pulls away in the second half. The total over 51 points is a safe bet also.

Prediction: Georgia by two scores.

There's an inordinate amount of variance in the early lines on this game. I'm on record predicting Miami winning the national championship. Notre Dame is also heavily in the conversation. The Fighting Irish have an easy schedule, ridiculously easy to be honest. BYU aside, this is their proving ground. They'll make the playoffs and be a threat, however no one really will know how good this team is until November. You'll see the line narrow considerably in the coming weeks. Miami is dynamic and will score points on anyone. Notre Dame's defense will be challenged for four quarters. The game is in South Bend. The home crowd needs to be full throat for 60 minutes to neutralize the Hurricanes offense. Darian Mensah shows out here, Miami with the (not an upset) win.

Prediction: Miami with an impressive performance to win. Take the over as well.

November 7th is one of those dream Saturdays. Alabama visits LSU, Oklahoma goes to Florida and the aforementioned Miami-Notre Dame clash takes place also.
For pure excitement though look no further than Ducks-Buckeyes. Talent, speed and playmakers litter the field. This is a No. 1 vs No. 2 matchup as of today and very well could be the same in November. You'll have several Heisman candidates, future number one picks and athletes you can only dream of having at your school going at it. Understandably there's no point total listed yet. I would put it around 57.5 today. That still may be a little low.

Prediction: Julian Sayin outduels Dante Moore in a thriller. Take the over no matter what it turns out to be.

I'd put Texas at a +3.5 favorite at the moment. LSU is the great unknown at this point. Lane Kiffin brings the swagger, bravado and attitude that will either bring great success or a train wreck. Either way, it will be fun. The game should be at night. There is absolutely nothing better than a night game in Tiger Stadium, live or on television. The atmosphere is otherworldly. If LSU lives up to or surpasses expectations, this will steal the 2026 show. If not, well I'll be content with hearing Callin' Baton Rouge at the beginning of the fourth quarter.

Prediction: LSU threatens an upset, tbd.

Fans whatever you do circle November 7th-no weddings, no funerals (unless it's yours). Tell the significant other to make plans for themselves. Make sure the grill works (or delivery is on time). Have your beverages cold. Wear the jersey. Send the kids away.

November isn't for a while yet, we have months to perfect the routine. Two-a-days help. Watch the side eye.

title: Purdue football stocks up on experience in secondary for 2026
description: Purdue needed major upgrades to its secondary after last season. The Boilermakers brought in several DBs with power conference experience.
fullText:
WEST LAFAYETTE – You could argue Purdue football's most important need in the offseason was in the secondary.

The Boilermakers made a concerted effort to lure experienced power conference defensive backs from the transfer portal, adding size and depth more so than at any other position.

Now, defensive passing game coordinator Charles Clark and defensive coordinator Kevin Kane have the task of finding who will play and where they'll play.

There's a lot of versatility among the group, and cross-training guys at safety, corner, and nickel provides flexibility.

It's hard to imagine Purdue won't be better in the secondary a season after the Boilers ranked 117th nationally in points per game allowed. Purdue totaled four interceptions all last season, ranking last in the Big Ten.

Who is back (2025 stats): Smiley Bradford, junior (30 tackles, 5 TFL, 1 INT, 6 PBU); Hudauri Hines, junior (33 tackles, 1.5 TFL, 1 INT, 8 PBU); Ryan Turner, senior (10 tackles, 0.5 sacks); Vi'Naz Cobb, sophomore (9 tackles); Traveon Wright, junior (7 tackles, 2 PBU); Maxwell Barbee, redshirt freshman; D'Mon Marable, junior (2 tackles); DJ Greene, redshirt freshman; Kaleb Richmond, junior; Zyntreacs Otey, redshirt freshman; Isaiah Needam, sophomore (6 tackles); Donivan Taylor, redshirt freshman

New faces: Jaden Mangham, senior (30 tackles, 2 TFL, 2 PBU in 2025 at Michigan), 2023 All-Big Ten honorable mention at Michigan State after making 53 tackles with 7 PBU and 4 INT); Jett Goldsberry, freshman; Mister Clark, junior (63 tackles, 6.5 TFL, 3 INT, 1 FF, first-team All-Conference USA in 2025 at Florida International); Don Saunders, junior (4 tackles, 2 PBU in 2025 at Utah, 2022 All-Big Sky at Cal Poly); Ta'Vari Hampton, sophomore (115 tackles, 19 TFL, 4 INT, 9 PBU, 2 FF in 2026 at Northeastern Oklahoma A&M, second-team NJCAA All-American); John Slaughter, senior (25 tackles, 2 INT, 1 FF in 2025 at Colorado, played 23 games over two seasons at Tennessee); Emoni Smith, freshman; Justin Denson Jr., sophomore (played 11 games over two seasons at Michigan State); Raderrion Daniels, freshman; Dax Noles, sophomore (61 tackles, 3 TFL, 4 INT, 2 FF in 2205 at Iowa Western; first-team NJCAA All-American)

More: Can production meet potential for Purdue football's defensive ends?

Hines is somewhat of a rarity among the defensive backs, now in his third season as a Boilermaker cornerback. He's had a lot of teammates, but may have found the yin to his yang in Saunders, a 6-foot-4 speedster now at his fourth school.

Those two have separated themselves as the best DBs on the outside.

"I think the biggest thing is they complement each other," defensive backs coach Charles Clark said. "They get on to each other. They coach each other. They teach each other. They motivate each other. When you have that on the outside, you feel comfortable about those guys going out there and just doing what they do."

The Boilermakers targeted defensive backs who've been through the wars.

In transfers Mangham, Clark, Denson, Slaughter, Noles, and Hampton, there are a lot of college games played, and all but Hampton have been at power conference football programs before.

But more than that, it was about finding players who fit Purdue's aggressive attack mode approach.

"One thing that made the bond easier here is we all want to win," Slaughter said. "A lot of guys have different stories from the schools they were at. Everybody is eager to work, and we have a point to prove."

Slaughter, Denson, and Mangham will all see action. Beyond that, there are a lot of options still vying for playing time.

"Our entire room, there's a lot of positionless players," Mangham said. "A lot of people can play everywhere."

More: Purdue football QB battle still isn't over

With all the experience, opportunities on Saturdays (and two Friday nights) may be scarce, but freshmen Emoni Smith and Jett Goldsberry have made plays throughout fall camp.

Smith's ability has overshadowed his 6-foot frame. Goldsberry was long committed to Mississippi, but Purdue was relentless in recruiting the Boilermaker legacy, whose father was a linebacker-turned-fullback at Purdue from 2000-04.

Goldsberry missed spring camp while rehabbing a torn ACL suffered during high school. Now healthy, he's quickly been thrown into the fire.

"We're kind of force-feeding him some reps right now," Charles Clark said. "Just to kind of see where he's at. ... I knew he had the talent in high school and was a guy we had to go to battle for in the recruiting game. He was committed to another school in the SEC for six months. Just persistence and relationship building and constant communication with him got that guy to come aboard and come be a part of something special here."

title: 4 most overrated college football teams entering 2026 season
description: Which of these 4 teams will fail to meet expectations?
fullText:
"OVER-RATED!" We've all heard the chant from the college football student sections as they look to heckle a visiting player or team. Sometimes, it's simply inaccurate and only serves to motivate the party in question, but other times, it's just correct.

Whether it be prior performance, name recognition, or splashy offseason "gets," some teams end up with a much higher public perception than their actual ability level, and end up, dare we say, overrated.

Here are the top-4 overrated teams heading into the 2026 season. Clap, clap, clap, clap, clap.

MORE: College Football conference power rankings ahead of 2026 Week 0

Jan 1, 2026; Pasadena, CA, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen Deboer looks on before the 2026 Rose Bowl and quarterfinal game of the College Football Playoff against the Indiana Hoosiers at Rose Bowl Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Under Nick Saban, the Crimson Tide were the most dominant program in college football. They got all the best recruits and won all of the big games. But Nick Saban isn't walking through that door. This is the Kalen DeBoer Alabama, and I believe that their previous history under Saban is carrying a lot of water with the national perception of how good this team is. T

he defense, which was just okay last year, has been gutted. Quarterback Ty Simpson covered up a lot of offensive issues last season, namely the complete and utter lack of a run game. Simpson is now a Los Angeles Ram, and the starting quarterback for 2026 has not yet been named. I'm just not seeing it with this team this year. Kalen DeBoer's seat is going to be getting awfully warm.

The Sooners rank in the top-10 in the first AP Poll of the season. On paper, it makes sense – they return their dynamic starting QB John Mateer, Brent Venables retained much of his coaching staff, and much of the nasty defense returns. So then why do most sportsbooks have Oklahoma's win total at 7.5? This tells us that Vegas thinks this is a 7-5 or 8-4 team, and top-10 teams don't end with fewer than 10 wins.

I'm on the side with Vegas. While they return a lot from last year, that was a team that had a pitiful run game and relied on an elite defense and kicker to win low-scoring, one-possession games. They were 4-1 last season when the margin of victory was 8 or fewer points. I'm not a believer in a team that may have returned a lot, but did not attempt to fix its flaws.

MORE: College Football top 25 power rankings ahead of 2026 Week 0

Jan 19, 2026; Miami Gardens, FL, USA; Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal against the Indiana Hoosiers during the College Football Playoff National Championship game at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images

What would be the perception of the Hurricanes if Miami had lost to Texas A&M in the first round of the College Football Playoff? Or if the CFP Committee didn't have Miami randomly leapfrog Notre Dame to get in the bracket? We would be looking at a team that has a history of losing games to inferior opponents thanks to baffling game-management decisions by Mario Cristobal, which they still did twice last season.

We would be looking at a team that has lost its cheat code – the elite pair of pass rushers, Rueben Bain and Akheem Mesidor, have gone to the NFL. You could argue that Darian Mensah is an improvement over Carson Beck at quarterback, but I think the run last season was a little fluky and I worry about how the loss of Bain and Mesidor will negatively impact the defense.

Out goes James Franklin, and in comes Matt Campbell, and what feels like the entirety of his starting lineup from Iowa State last season. So why do we think that a team that went 8-4 in the Big 12 is going to all of a sudden be a top-15 team just because they wear a different jersey?

I'm not buying it. The counter-argument would be that Penn State drew a Charmin Extra-Soft Big 10 conference schedule that dodges Ohio State, Oregon, and Indiana. They will likely be favored in 10 or 11 games this season, but that doesn't mean that they are actually a quality football team.

title: NY Giants-Miami Dolphins joint practice: ‘Rules of engagement’ will be in place
description: John Harbaugh wants players on both teams to protect each other.
fullText:
Recently, I was listening to Sirius XM NFL Radio while driving to New York Giants practice. The host of the show (I see you, Bob Papa) was basically doing play-by-play of the fights breaking out during a joint practice between the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

I relay that story because fights seem to be commonplace during these joint practices, and the Giants are participating in one with the Miami Dolphins on Thursday in Miami.

Joint practices, of course, are not the controlled situations teams can create for their players during normal practices.

With that in mind, I asked Giants head coach John Harbaugh, a veteran of many of these situations, if there was a way a head coach could try to keep his players safe during a situation where he isn't in charge of every player on the field.

Welcome to the 'Rules of Engagement'.

"We'll have rules of engagement, we'll call it," Harbaugh said. "Talked to Coach Hafley. He talks to his team. We talk to our team. We have the same rules of engagement."

Harbaugh said those rules will include, and probably emphasize, that defenders getting anywhere the opposing quarterback is strictly verboten.

"It'll be the same that we use in our practice. It'll be probably more to the quarterback," Harbaugh said. "We'll emphasize protecting each other's quarterbacks even more, because as soon as somebody gets close, and the other team's going to talk about getting close, and we can't have that, nobody can get close to the quarterback. That's going to be a major point of emphasis."

There will be other rules of engagement.

"We're going to stay off the ground, and we're going to be looking for no blindside shots of any kind. We're not looking for that," Harbaugh said." It's a front-up tackle. That's kind of a front-up type of thud, wrap you can do, but it won't be side shots and things like that. That's the goal.

"So, we want to protect them as much as we protect our own players, and we want them to protect our players as much as they would protect their own players."

This will be a single practice in advance of Saturday's preseason game. What is Harbaugh's goal?

"I'm looking to get a good practice against a different team," Harbaugh said. "You get an opportunity to go against different players, different schemes, and evaluate your guys along those lines. It's good. It's just nice to see a different format, different plays, different players.

"And it's fun. It's more interesting. It's not another practice day for the guys. They're going against a new team."

Nabers, on the comeback trail from a pair of surgeries to repair a torn ACL, just began participating in a handful of team drills this week. He has been wearing a red, non-contact jersey.

Nabers will travel with the Giants to Miami, but won't take part in team drills on Thursday or play in Saturday's preseason game.

The Giants want to get Nabers involved in some degree of physicality in a controlled practice setting before exposing him to defenders on other teams.

"He won't go through the rest of the summer in a red jersey," Harbaugh said. "No, he'll be out of a red jersey before he plays in a game. He's going to have to get bumped around and hit and fronted up so he knows how to, you just have to feel that and know how to deal with it to protect yourself."

That just isn't going to happen in Miami.

[NOTE: Practice begins today at 9:30 a.m.]

title: Barcelona key defender will be available vs Elche after not playing in Gamper Trophy match
description: Pau Cubarsi was the only FC Barcelona first-team player included in the squad who did not play a single minute in the Joan Gamper Trophy match against Al Ahly on Wednesday.However, according to SPORT,...
fullText:
Pau Cubarsi was the only FC Barcelona first-team player included in the squad who did not play a single minute in the Joan Gamper Trophy match against Al Ahly on Wednesday.

However, according to SPORT, Hansi Flick's decision to not use the World Cup winner should not raise any concerns. The youngster is expected to be available for the La Liga opener against Elche come Sunday.

The centre-back remained on the bench simply to avoid overloading himself ahead of the imminent start of the new season.

Cubarsi played all 750 minutes of Spain's eight matches at the World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, completing the full 90 minutes in the seven games leading up to the final, where he also played the entire extra time.

The La Masia defender was awarded the tournament's Best Young Player prize. He formed an outstanding partnership with Aymeric Laporte, conceding just one goal throughout the World Cup, against Belgium.

Cubarsi played every minute for Spain at the World Cup. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images)

That workload took a significant physical toll, so a gradual return to action is now considered the right option for the youngster.

Cubarsi was unavailable for the pre-season friendly against Birmingham City and the triangular tournament featuring Nottingham Forest and Udinese. His return came against Basel, where he played 19 minutes.

Since then, he has continued training, but Flick did not want to take the slightest risk with him in the Gamper Trophy, despite the player having no significant physical problems. The coach is simply managing his workload.

Cubarsi will be an undisputed starter once Flick believes he is ready and there is no risk of injury. For now, he will be in the squad for Sunday's match against Elche, although he is not expected to start.

Will be available for the season opener. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

That leaves Flick with a decision over who will partner Gerard Martín at centre-back. Eric Garcia will start at right-back at the beginning of the season, while Alejandro Balde will occupy the left side.

In central defence, Flick tested Jules Kounde against Al Ahly, but Andreas Christensen has also made an excellent start to the summer.

The dilemma for Flick, therefore, is whether to move Kounde back to his original position at centre-back or maintain Christensen's place.

title: Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Players to consider for GW1 of FPL

The 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League season is here and ready to kick off on Friday night as FPL managers finalise their team before the GW1 deadline.

Fantasy Premier League begins with several highly appealing options across the price points. Let's look at some of the players that one must consider based on fixtures and form.

Haaland is the most expensive player in FPL history at £15.5m, but his record makes him difficult to ignore. He scored 239 FPL points last season and remains Manchester City's main penalty-box threat. His goalscoring volume, penalty responsibility and captaincy potential make him one of the safest premium choices for Gameweek 1. Although his price requires sacrifices elsewhere, Haaland can provide an immediate advantage with Manchester City's favourable fixtures.

Wirtz is priced at £7.5m and offers an attractive route into Liverpool's attack. He scored 125 FPL points last season and has the technical quality to operate as a primary creator or advanced midfielder. His ability to produce key passes, assists and occasional goals gives him a strong ceiling at a mid-range price. Wirtz is also an appealing alternative for managers who want Liverpool attacking coverage without paying premium prices for every forward option.

Calafiori costs £5.5m and provides a potential route into Arsenal's defence. Arsenal defenders can offer returns through clean sheets, bonus points and set-piece situations, while Calafiori's ability to contribute in possession gives him additional attacking potential. His price is higher than the cheapest defenders, but regular starts and Arsenal's defensive strength could make him a useful long-term asset rather than merely a one-week pick.

Bryan Mbeumo is priced at £8.0m for the new FPL campaign. He scored 148 points last season, highlighting his ability to combine goals, assists and regular involvement. His appeal will depend heavily on his position and role in Manchester United's attack, but with Benjamin Sesko sidelined, Mbeumo could operate in an advanced position through the middle, increasing his potential. At £8.0m, Mbeumo is an enticing mid-priced midfielder with significant ownership and points potential.

João Pedro is priced at £7.5m and scored 177 FPL points last season, making him one of the standout forwards in the new game. His price is unchanged despite that strong total, which keeps him within reach for managers building a balanced squad. He's been in fine form during the pre-season, scoring seven times, and has been handed Chelsea's number nine shirt for the new season, underlining his status in Xabi Alonso's plans. His popularity reflects the probability that he becomes the central figure in Chelsea's attacking structure.
